reason: Settling dust into the young star's disk seems like a useful first step toward gathering rocky pebbles.
expectation: I expect the falling dust to join the disk, perhaps preparing grains to stick together.

alternatives.reason: Inward-moving icy grains might also contribute to the warm disk, but I want to establish the dust supply first.

effect: The dust has settled into the disk's crowded middle plane, where it can meet other grains.
reaction: The role of gas drag in concentrating the grains is interesting.
reason: Slowly meeting grains seem likely to stick to the settled dust and advance the pebble goal.
expectation: I expect some grains to stick together into larger aggregates, though they may not yet be pebbles.

alternatives.reason: A fast collision may address the other goal, but I want to try gradual growth first.

effect: Gentle collisions produced fragile clumps, but they are not yet rocky pebbles.
reaction: The contrast between sticking and potentially destructive collisions is clear.
reason: The clumps are fragile, so a fast encounter seems relevant to the hard-collision goal.
expectation: I expect the fast grains to break up the clumps, leaving smaller fragments.

alternatives.reason: Warming icy grains may advance the pebble goal, but I want to see what happens to the fragile clumps first.

effect: The fast collision shattered the clumps into smaller grains, completing the hard-collision goal.
reaction: The reversal of the earlier growth was satisfying and predictable.
reason: The warm inner disk seems relevant to gathering rocky pebbles from the inward-moving grains.
expectation: I expect the ice coatings to vaporize in the warmth, leaving rocky material behind, though not necessarily pebbles yet.

alternatives.reason: Slow encounters might let the shattered grains stick together again, but I want to see what warming the icy grains does.

effect: The warmth evaporated the ice, leaving rocky grains available for growth.
reaction: The distinction between evaporation and disappearance is clear.
reason: Slow encounters may help the newly exposed rocky grains stick together toward the pebble goal.
expectation: I expect the rocky grains to form larger aggregates, possibly pebbles.

alternatives.reason: The shattered grains might also regrow through slow encounters, but the exposed rocky grains seem more directly relevant to the warm-disk goal.

effect: Gentle encounters built the dry grains into rocky pebbles, completing the chapter; further sticking alone is not enough to make planets.
reaction: The qualification about the limits of sticking made the result more interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Shattering the fluffy clumps made the contrast between gentle growth and destructive collisions tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: Settling the dust was useful setup, but less engaging than seeing the contrasting collision outcomes.

surprise.text: The pebbles still cannot grow all the way into planets through sticking alone.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the choices followed the goals and the described behavior of the grains.

continue.text: Yes. I'd be curious to see what processes take rocky pebbles further toward forming planets.
